facts.value: Founded by Jacob Albright, a German Lutheran of Pennsylvania, through a mission among his fellow-countrymen. Its government and theology are close to those of the Methodist Episcopal Church. It took its present name in 1818 and divided in 1891.

citations.excerpt: rules of government were adopted somewhat similar to those of the Methodist Episcopal Church. The theological standards of the two bodies are also in close agreement.
In 1807 Albright was appointed bishop of the community, which adopted its present name in 1818.
In 1891 a long internal controversy resulted in a division.
